root_cause.text: `cgroup_rmdir()` was waiting for dying tasks to leave the cgroup before killing the cgroup_subsys_state (css) `percpu_ref`, but tasks past `exit_signals()` can still remain linked in `cset->tasks` until `finish_task_switch()`, so `->css_offline()` could run before the cgroup was actually depopulated.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `cgroup_drain_dying()` wait from `cgroup_rmdir()` and changes teardown to split into `kill_css_sync()` plus deferred `kill_css_finish()`, with `cgroup_finish_destroy()` only queued when `!cgroup_is_populated(cgrp)`; the commit message says “Defer css percpu_ref kill on rmdir until cgroup is depopulated” and explains that tasks “past exit_signals() linger on cset->tasks until their final context switch,” which made the old rmdir wait/kill ordering unsafe.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace the cgroup dying-task wait queue with deferred destroy work so css teardown is postponed until the cgroup is fully depopulated.
intent_record.what: In struct cgroup, the field `wait_queue_head_t dying_populated_waitq` and its comment were removed, and replaced with a new comment plus a `struct work_struct finish_destroy_work` member.
intent_record.how: This changes the cgroup teardown mechanism from waiting on a dedicated wait queue for dying tasks to a deferred work item that finishes destruction only after the cgroup has been depopulated, altering when csses are actually killed after removal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Split cgroup CSS destruction into distinct synchronous and completion مراحل by introducing new helper declarations and removing the old single kill entry point.
intent_record.what: The function prototype `kill_css(struct cgroup_subsys_state *css)` was removed from the declarations near the top of the file and replaced by three new forward declarations: `cgroup_finish_destroy(struct cgroup *cgrp)`, `kill_css_sync(struct cgroup_subsys_state *css)`, and `kill_css_finish(struct cgroup_subsys_state *css)`.
intent_record.how: This changes the cgroup teardown API surface by splitting the previous `kill_css` operation into separate synchronous and finish phases, plus a cgroup-level destroy completion helper. At runtime, destruction logic can now be sequenced more explicitly instead of relying on one monolithic kill path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Queue deferred cgroup destruction when an offlined cgroup's subtree becomes empty so the one-shot teardown path is correctly executed.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added inside cgroup_update_populated() before cgroup1_check_for_release(): it checks whether the cgroup was previously populated and is now offline via !css_is_online(&cgrp->self), then calls cgroup_get(cgrp) and queues cgrp->finish_destroy_work on cgroup_offline_wq with a WARN_ON_ONCE() if queue_work() fails. A comment was also added explaining that this handles a subtree that has just emptied below an offlined cgroup and that the transition is one-shot.
intent_record.how: When a cgroup becomes empty after its own css has already been offlined, the code now schedules deferred destruction work instead of relying only on the normal populated-state transition. This ensures the destroy path runs for that one-time transition and keeps the cgroup alive long enough for the queued work to complete.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a workqueue handler to safely finish cgroup destruction under lock and release the cgroup reference afterward.
intent_record.what: A new static workqueue callback function, `cgroup_finish_destroy_work_fn()`, was added. It derives a `struct cgroup *` from the embedded `finish_destroy_work` using `container_of()`, takes the cgroup lock, calls `cgroup_finish_destroy(cgrp)`, releases the lock, and then drops the cgroup reference with `cgroup_put(cgrp)`.
intent_record.how: This adds deferred execution for the cgroup destruction finalization path: the cleanup now runs in workqueue context under the proper lock and ensures the cgroup object is reference-counted correctly while destruction completes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace incorrect waitqueue initialization with work item setup so cgroup destruction completion is handled through deferred work.
intent_record.what: In cgroup housekeeping initialization, the call to initialize `cgrp->dying_populated_waitq` was removed and replaced with `INIT_WORK(&cgrp->finish_destroy_work, cgroup_finish_destroy_work_fn);` while `offline_waitq` and `release_agent_work` initialization remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cgroup setup now prepares a deferred work item for finishing cgroup destruction instead of initializing the `dying_populated_waitq` wait queue at this point. This changes the initialized object from a wait queue to a workqueue task, enabling destruction completion to be handled asynchronously by `cgroup_finish_destroy_work_fn`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Split CSS teardown into synchronized and ավարտed kill steps when disabling a cgroup control state.
intent_record.what: In the cgroup control disable path, a call to `kill_css(css)` was replaced with two calls: `kill_css_sync(css)` followed by `kill_css_finish(css)`.
intent_record.how: When a cgroup subsystem state is being disabled and the CSS has a parent but is no longer in the subsystem mask, the code now performs the CSS kill in two explicit phases instead of a single call. This changes the teardown path to synchronize and complete the kill operation before continuing, which can prevent premature cleanup or lifecycle ordering issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the css destruction comment to reference the correct implementation function.
intent_record.what: The comment in the css destruction sequence was changed to say that stage 1 is "Implemented in kill_css_finish()" instead of "Implemented in kill_css()"; no executable code was modified.
intent_record.how: This does not alter runtime behavior. It only updates documentation to point to the correct function responsible for initiating percpu_ref killing during css destruction, reducing confusion for readers and maintainers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the comment to reference the correct css teardown helper function.
intent_record.what: The comment in `css_killed_work_fn()` was updated, changing the referenced function name from `kill_css()` to `kill_css_finish()`.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it only corrects the documentation to reflect the current lifecycle function responsible for finishing css destruction and dropping the css reference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename and re-document the css teardown helper to reflect that it performs the synchronous part of destruction.
intent_record.what: The function comment was rewritten to describe a synchronous teardown helper, and the function was renamed from `kill_css` to `kill_css_sync`. The old detailed description of asynchronous destruction behavior was removed and replaced with a brief reference to `cgroup_destroy_locked()`.
intent_record.how: This change is primarily semantic and structural: it clarifies that this helper only performs the synchronous portion of cgroup subsystem state teardown and no longer advertises the full destruction flow. Runtime behavior is not directly changed by the shown hunk, but the renamed function better reflects its role in the teardown sequence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the extra reference hold and confirmed ref-kill step from css teardown so cgroup killing can proceed without waiting for per-CPU death confirmation.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a block from kill_css() that previously took an extra css reference with css_get(css) and then called percpu_ref_kill_and_confirm(&css->refcnt, css_killed_ref_fn), along with the associated explanatory comments. The remaining code now proceeds directly from css_clear_dir(css) to incrementing css->cgroup->nr_dying_subsys[ss->id].
intent_record.how: At runtime, kill_css() no longer explicitly pins the css base reference or waits for per-CPU refcount death confirmation before continuing. This changes the teardown path so it advances without the extra reference-management and confirmation step that previously delayed later offlining/freeing-related transitions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix cgroup destruction to reject busy cgroups based on live tasks and to defer css offlining until percpu refcount killing is fully confirmed.
intent_record.what: The patch introduces a new static helper, `kill_css_finish(struct cgroup_subsys_state *css)`, which checks whether the css refcount is already dying and, if not, takes an extra base reference and calls `percpu_ref_kill_and_confirm(&css->refcnt, css_killed_ref_fn)`. It also rewrites the `cgroup_destroy_locked()` kernel-doc comment to describe a three-stage destruction flow, and changes the `cgroup_destroy_locked()` prologue by adding `css_task_iter`/`task_struct` locals and replacing the old `if (cgroup_is_populated(cgrp)) return -EBUSY;` check with a task iteration over `cgrp->self` that returns `-EBUSY` if any task is found.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cgroup destruction now explicitly verifies whether the cgroup itself still has a live task visible through the css task iterator rather than relying only on the populated flag, preventing teardown while a userspace-visible task remains. The new helper defers the second half of css teardown until the percpu refcount is confirmed killed on all CPUs, preserving the css base reference until after `->css_offline()` can safely run and ensuring `css_tryget_online()` cannot succeed before offlining begins.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch cgroup destruction to synchronous css killing so all css objects are fully torn down before the cgroup is removed.
intent_record.what: In cgroup_destroy_locked(), the call inside the for_each_css(css, ssid, cgrp) loop was changed from kill_css(css) to kill_css_sync(css), and the preceding comment "initiate massacre of all css's" was removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cgroup destruction now waits for synchronous css teardown for each css in the cgroup instead of triggering the previous asynchronous kill path. This changes the destruction flow to ensure css objects are fully killed before proceeding with directory cleanup and removal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor cgroup teardown to finish destruction immediately once the cgroup is empty, replacing the old dying-task drain logic.
intent_record.what: The code removes the entire cgroup_drain_dying() function, which previously checked for visible tasks, waited on dying tasks via a waitqueue, and returned busy/error status. In cgroup_destroy_locked(), after killing the self reference, it now conditionally calls a new cgroup_finish_destroy(cgrp) helper when the cgroup is no longer populated. The new helper is introduced as a void function that iterates over all css entries in the cgroup and calls kill_css_finish(css) for each one.
intent_record.how: Destruction now splits into an earlier lock-held teardown step and a deferred finish step that runs immediately once the cgroup becomes empty. This changes rmdir behavior by no longer waiting for PF_EXITING tasks to drain inside the old busy-check path; instead, the final per-css cleanup is performed directly when the subtree is empty, aligning destruction completion with population state and simplifying teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify cgroup_rmdir by removing the drain step and destroying the cgroup directly before tracing successful removal.
intent_record.what: In cgroup_rmdir(), the call to cgroup_drain_dying(cgrp) and its surrounding conditional were removed. The function now calls cgroup_destroy_locked(cgrp) directly, and if that succeeds it still emits TRACE_CGROUP_PATH(rmdir, cgrp) before unlocking and returning.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cgroup removal no longer waits for or explicitly drains dying cgroups before attempting destruction. The rmdir path now proceeds straight to locked destruction, which changes the teardown sequence and likely removes an unnecessary or redundant pre-destruction step.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused local variable from do_cgroup_task_dead.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration `struct cgrp_cset_link *link;` was removed from `do_cgroup_task_dead(struct task_struct *tsk)`. No other code in the hunk was changed.
intent_record.how: This has no runtime behavioral effect by itself; it only eliminates an unused local variable from the function, leaving execution logic unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the direct wakeup of cgroup dying-population waiters from task death handling.
intent_record.what: The code block in `do_cgroup_task_dead()` that iterated over `cset->cgrp_links` and conditionally called `wake_up(&link->cgrp->dying_populated_waitq)` was removed, along with its accompanying comment about kicking `cgroup_drain_dying()` waiters.
intent_record.how: At runtime, task death no longer directly wakes waiters on each linked cgroup's `dying_populated_waitq` from this function, so that notification path is eliminated here and must be handled elsewhere if still needed.

The vulnerability stems from using cgroup_has_tasks() as the depopulation indicator. Because this state lags behind task exit, it can cause cgroup_rmdir() to wait on the wrong condition and then kill the css percpu_ref before all tasks have actually left.
